explanation: Friction comes in two flavors. Push gently and STATIC friction silently matches your push so nothing moves — but only up to a ceiling f_s,max = mu_s·N. Slide mu_s up to raise that ceiling. Once your push exceeds it the block breaks free and KINETIC friction f_k = mu_k·N takes over; because mu_k is a bit smaller, the block lurches forward. Heavier mass m raises N = mg, so both frictions scale up with it.
bullets: Static friction self-adjusts up to f_s,max = mu_s·N — it never exceeds your push.
Once moving, kinetic friction is constant: f_k = mu_k·N, and mu_k ≤ mu_s.
Both scale with the normal force N = mg, not with contact area.
